Context/method: UK student accommodation; online attribute analysis
What it does NOT justify: Displaying every possible attribute or claiming one universal preference order.

Context/method: Edinburgh; in-depth interviews with students experiencing housing precarity
Main contribution: More PBSA does not automatically solve affordability-led housing precarity.
What it supports: Critical distinction between supply quantity and affordability.
What it does NOT justify: Using bed growth as proof that the housing problem is solved.
FairNest design implication: Compare affordability and booking cash, not just availability.

Main contribution: PBSA growth is embedded in planning, investment and constructions of student housing.
What it supports: Critical treatment of PBSA as a governed market form.
What it does NOT justify: Assuming professionally managed PBSA is automatically optimal.
FairNest design implication: Do not privilege tenure type in ranking.
Transfer limitation: Planning/legal emphasis rather than user testing.

Main contribution: Students are treated as a distinct and sometimes excluded housing population through regulation.
What it supports: Agreement context matters for housing choice.
What it does NOT justify: Applying one private-rental rule set across all student housing.
Transfer limitation: Policy analysis; not a behavioural experiment.

Context/method: Scotland; 45 student interviews across three catchments
Main contribution: Student accommodation is experienced as home; emotions, shared living and inclusion matter.

Context/method: Australia; mixed methods with international students
Main contribution: Accommodation, location and perceived safety relate to wellbeing.
What it supports: Importance of location/context in decision support.
What it does NOT justify: UK prevalence estimates or direct causal effects.

Main contribution: Precarious/expensive accommodation can affect academic experience.
What it does NOT justify: Assuming the same effect size in Coventry.
FairNest design implication: Treat booking cash and total cost as salient.

Main contribution: Signals differ in credibility and verifiability under information asymmetry.
What it supports: Source provenance, check dates and verifiable evidence.
What it does NOT justify: A generic 'verified' badge as proof of safety.
FairNest design implication: Evidence provenance rather than opaque certification.

Main contribution: Trust and perceived risk shape online purchase decisions.
What it supports: Need to expose evidence and uncertainty before commitment.
What it does NOT justify: Claim that FairNest will increase conversion without testing.
FairNest design implication: Explain why a field is believed and flag missing data.

Main contribution: Platform participation depends on value/price structure across both sides.
What it supports: Free student core with provider-side monetisation logic.
What it does NOT justify: Proof that the proposed prices are acceptable.
FairNest design implication: Keep provider payments separate from organic ranking.
Transfer limitation: Foundational theory; no FairNest WTP evidence.
